title: How the rook moves
outcomes: Taps every square a rook can reach, including captures and blocked lines
Predicts whether a line is blocked before moving
Says why a rook cannot reach a square that is off its rank and file

steps.text: The **rook** moves in straight lines: along a rank (sideways) or a file (up and down), as far as it likes. It cannot jump over pieces. To **capture**, it lands on an enemy piece and takes it off the board. It can never land on a square holding its own piece.

steps.caption: The rook slides until something is in the way. It can take the black pawn on d7, but not go past it.

steps.text: Before you move a rook, ask three questions. Is the square on its rank or its file? Is anything standing between? Whose piece, if any, is on the square? Empty or enemy: allowed, and a captured piece ends the slide. Your own piece: not allowed. These are rules of the game, not rules of thumb, so they hold in every position.

steps.title: Same rook, one change
steps.prompt: A black pawn appears on d6. Predict first: can the rook still reach d8? Then see what a pawn on e6 does instead.
In the silent round, name one answer that was a guess. Which line did you not trace to its end: a rank, a file or a diagonal? Rate how sure you were overall. (low / medium / high)
